title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
gist: Alphabet's Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% to almost $128 billion, but EPS of $2.12 missed the $3.02 consensus, net income fell nearly $9 billion, and the stock dropped about 12%. Google admitted AI Mode queries monetize worse than web search, search growth slowed to 12% with flat search revenue, and capex keeps rising toward $300B+ of AI investment in 2027.

insights.claim: Alphabet took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, up 25 percent year over year, but net income of over $26 billion was almost $9 billion lower than a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Revenue growth isn't translating to profit as AI costs bite.
insights.quote: While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower.

insights.claim: Google reported EPS of $2.12 versus a $3.02 consensus, and the stock fell almost 12 percent, one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: A large EPS miss reset market expectations on AI-era profitability.
insights.quote: Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02.

insights.claim: Google Cloud beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in quarterly revenue, about $1 billion above analyst estimates, and cloud revenue more than doubled over the past year.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Cloud is the main bull case supporting AI spending.
insights.quote: Google’s Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue.

insights.claim: Search volume grew 12 percent year over year in Q3, down from 17 percent in Q2 and 19 percent in Q1, and search revenue was flat.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Core search engine growth is decelerating sharply.
insights.quote: In the last quarter, Google saw search grow by 12 percent versus last year.
